source: NCERT Class XI, Themes in World History, Ch. 1 (Writing and City Life).

sections.heading: 1. Mesopotamia — Land and People
points: **Mesopotamia** = 'land between two rivers' (**Tigris and Euphrates**), in present-day **Iraq**; one of the earliest urban civilisations.
Regions: **Sumer and Akkad** (south), **Babylonia** (centre), **Assyria** (north).
Fertile alluvial soil supported agriculture; key to city life were **agriculture, trade and writing**.

sections.heading: 2. Cities and Urbanisation
points: The **city of Uruk** was among the earliest; cities grew from temple towns, trade centres and imperial capitals.
**Division of labour** and interdependence marked city life; the **temple (ziggurat)** was central to economic and religious life.
**Warka Head** and seals show artistic skill; the wheel and the plough aided development.

sections.heading: 3. Writing and the Cuneiform Script
points: The world's **first writing** system was **cuneiform** (wedge-shaped), written on **clay tablets** with a reed stylus, from about **3200 BCE**.
Writing began for **keeping records** (of trade, transactions, rations), then extended to law, literature and administration.
Writing was in the **Sumerian language**, later **Akkadian**; being literate was rare and prestigious.
The **Epic of Gilgamesh** — a famous Mesopotamian literary work (includes a flood story).

sections.heading: 4. Legacy of Mesopotamia
points: Mesopotamians contributed to **mathematics and astronomy** — division of the year, the **60-unit system** (60 minutes in an hour, 360 degrees in a circle), and calculations still used today.
Advances in the **calendar, time-keeping and the zodiac**.
Their urban culture, writing, law and learning influenced later civilisations.

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Mesopotamia = between Tigris and Euphrates (modern Iraq).
First writing = cuneiform (wedge-shaped) on clay tablets (~3200 BCE).
Writing began for keeping records/accounts of trade.
Epic of Gilgamesh = famous Mesopotamian epic (flood story).
Legacy: 60-based time system (60 minutes, 360 degrees), astronomy, calendar.

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: Mesopotamia lies between the **Tigris and Euphrates** (not Nile — that's Egypt).
**Cuneiform** was **wedge-shaped**, written on **clay tablets**.
The division of the hour into **60 minutes** comes from Mesopotamia.
The **Epic of Gilgamesh** is Mesopotamian (not Greek).
